title: Preparation for Behavioural Tests in Mice
author: Amandine EVEN

steps.title: Prepare Experimental Groups
steps.instruction: Organize mice into groups while maintaining blinding and balanced distribution.

substeps.instruction: Ensure the experimenter is blind to the treatment and genotype of the mice.
For large groups, have a third party divide mice into three or more groups, ensuring an almost equal number of control and treated mice for each genotype.

steps.title: Plan Testing Schedule
steps.instruction: Establish a consistent sequence and timing for behavioral tests.

substeps.instruction: Maintain the same sequence of tests across all groups.
Schedule extensive tasks on separate days (e.g., open field and rotarod on different days).
Limit experiment duration to under 4 hours per batch to avoid light cycle phase differences.
Maintain consistent start and end working hours throughout the experiment period.

steps.title: Prepare Testing Environment
steps.instruction: Set up equipment and personal hygiene to minimize animal stress.

substeps.instruction: Plug in and start all necessary apparatus before moving mice into the manipulation room to avoid noise (e.g., rotarod) and difficulty locating items under red light.
Avoid using perfume, body lotion, or after-shave on days of handling or testing.

steps.title: Acclimatize Mice to Handler
steps.instruction: Handle mice daily to minimize stress before starting behavioral experiments.

substeps.instruction: Handle mice once a day for at least 5 days prior to experiments.
Spend an almost equal amount of time with each mouse, at least 00:10:00 per mouse per day.

steps.title: Coordinate with Light Cycle
steps.instruction: Perform experiments in alignment with the light-dark cycle.

substeps.instruction: Preferably perform experiments in an inverted light-dark cycle.
Start behavioral work at least one hour after the light-dark cycle change.
Avoid working with mice immediately after the light-dark transition.
